action: Poste Italiane customers: be wary of emails, calls or texts that use your name, contact details or contract information; do not share credentials.
date_note: Date of the forum post the article describes; Cybersecurity360 published November 19. Article gives the forum post as Tuesday 17 Nov and elsewhere as 18 Nov; not resolved.
exec: Customer contracts and contact details tied to a digital-signature service were reportedly leaked, raising phishing and fraud risk for customers of a major Italian provider.
plain: Poste Italiane told an Italian news site it had a data breach affecting a limited number of people, reported as over 1,500 customers. Names, emails and contract documents were reportedly exposed; Poste says payment credentials are safe.
summary: Cybersecurity360 reports that Poste Italiane confirmed a breach affecting a limited number of people on first analysis, with checks continuing. The article gives about 1,500 customers, attributing it to Poste, and elsewhere says over 1,500. About 1 GB of files, which the outlet says appear tied to PosteCert, include names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and contract documents. Poste is reported to say passwords and payment credentials are safe.
title: Poste Italiane confirms data breach; report puts it at over 1,500 customers

validation.note: Reviewer re-read Cybersecurity360 (19 Nov): limited number on first analysis; about 1,500 attributed to Poste, over 1,500 in outlet text; PosteCert is the outlet's inference; passwords and payment safe (paraphrase); forum post 17 vs 18 Nov unresolved; user flex22. Single source.

review.note: Summary wrongly said Poste gave no count; Cybersecurity360 attributes about 1,500 to Poste and says over 1,500 itself. Corrected. Other facts match: limited number, PosteCert as outlet inference, 1 GB, flex22; forum date 17 vs 18 Nov unresolved in article.
